Cost: renaming the slug is one keystroke plus Save, silently invalidating every bookmark, invite link and deep link into the workspace, with none of the caution the pane demonstrably knows how to write.
findings.recommendation: Add helper text under Slug stating that existing links stop working, and require a confirmation step showing old and new URL. If old slugs redirect, say so — that turns a scary change into a safe one.

findings.title: Destructive actions get inconsistent protection: Delete Server is a Danger Zone, Remove Admin is a plain outline button
findings.evidence: 17-server-profile.aria.txt:96-105 gives deletion an icon-marked "Danger Zone" section, a warning paragraph and a red 'button "Delete Server"'. Revoking an admin's privileges gets 'button "Remove Admin" [ref=e231]' (19-administration.aria.txt:102) — default outline styling, no section warning, no confirmation signal in the label or via aria-haspopup, flush right on a member row. Neither button reports [cursor=pointer] in the snapshot, while 'link "Documentation" [ref=e98] [cursor=pointer]' and the Appearance switch do — so the hover cursor does not change on the destructive controls either. Cost: a mis-click on a member row strips admin from an agent that may be running workspace onboarding (Cindy is the configured Human Onboarding Agent, 19-administration.aria.txt:164).
findings.recommendation: Tier destructive actions explicitly: irreversible (Delete Server) gets type-to-confirm; reversible-but-privileged (Remove Admin) gets a confirmation popover naming the member and the consequence, plus danger styling. Restore `cursor: pointer` on all buttons — currently the only hover affordance in Settings is on one link and one switch.

findings.title: Yellow #FFD440 means "selected" everywhere except on the Notifications badge, where it means "off"
findings.evidence: Sampled fills are identical (#FFD440) for the selected "Medium" font-size chip (15-appearance), the selected "Yearly" billing chip (18-billing), the selected "Marketplace" tab (20-applications) — and for the "DISABLED" status badge on 16-notifications, whose ARIA is 'generic [ref=e132]: Disabled' (16-notifications.aria.txt:81). Cost: the yellow pill reads as an active/selected chip in the exact spot users scan for on/off state, so push being off can be misread as on; the user then wonders why nothing arrives.
findings.recommendation: Give status badges their own neutral-vs-positive scale (grey "Off", green "On") distinct from the yellow selection token, and put the meaning in the text — "Push: off" rather than a bare "DISABLED".

findings.title: Billing defaults to the largest commitment and quotes a price it does not charge
findings.evidence: 'radio "Yearly Save 12%" [checked] [ref=e210]' is pre-selected (18-billing.aria.txt:140) and Seats to buy is pre-filled with "2" (line 149). The helper text says "Each seat is $10/month" (line 150) while the checkout summary total reads "$240 / year" struck against "$211.20 / year" (lines 169-170). Cost: a user who reads "$10/month", sees 2 seats and presses "Upgrade to Pro" commits to a $211.20 annual charge, not $20. The monthly figure is the only price stated in the form itself; the annual figure appears only in a side panel.
findings.recommendation: State the charge in the primary flow: put "You will be charged $211.20 today, then annually" directly above the Upgrade button and carry the amount in the button label. Default to Monthly, or if Yearly stays default, show both totals inline beside the two radios.

findings.title: Seat capacity is stated ambiguously and the checkout summary repeats the ambiguity instead of resolving it
findings.evidence: "2 seats selected. Each seat covers 1 human or 10 agents. Current usage requires at least 2 seats. Each seat is $10/month." (18-billing.aria.txt:150), and the summary restates "Capacity / up to 2 Humans / or 20 Agents" (lines 164-165). Neither says whether a mixed team of 1 human + 10 agents fits in 2 seats or 1, nor how the "at least 2" was derived from actual membership. Cost: on the only screen that takes money, the buyer cannot compute the seat count they need and will over- or under-buy.
findings.recommendation: Show the derivation — "You currently have 1 human and 1 agent → 2 seats required" — and express capacity as a single consumable with a live meter rather than an unexplained "or".

findings.title: MCP Servers explains none of its own vocabulary and carries no trust statement
findings.evidence: The pane's entire explanation is "Configure the MCP catalog, credentials, and provider connections for this Raft Server." (21-mcp.aria.txt:80) and the empty state "Add a Streamable HTTP server or start from a recommended integration." (line 84). "MCP" is never expanded, "Streamable HTTP server" is unglossed, there is no link to https://docs.raft.build from this pane, and nothing states which agents gain access to a connected server or where credentials are stored. The recommended entries describe only the vendor's capability — "Search and update the Notion workspace you authorize." (line 96). Cost: an admin wires a live Notion or Linear credential into the workspace with no statement of blast radius, on a pane strictly riskier than Applications — which does get a trust line.
findings.recommendation: Open the pane with one plain sentence: what an MCP server is, that adding one lets this workspace's agents call those tools, and who can use it. Add a docs link. Add per-server disclosure of which agents may invoke it and how credentials are held.

findings.title: Pre-join Agreement can be required, but its text cannot be read or written from the pane
findings.evidence: The section offers exactly one control — 'checkbox "Require agreement before joining New invite-link and community joins must accept the current version before membership is created." [ref=e292]' — plus "Saving creates a new version; previous accepted versions remain auditable." and a disabled Save (19-administration.aria.txt:144-150). There is no textarea, no preview, no "current version" link. Cost: an admin can gate all new joins on a document they cannot see, and the copy's reference to "the current version" points at content with no representation on screen.
findings.recommendation: Put the agreement body in this section — an editor showing the current version, its number and effective date, and a preview of what a joiner sees. Requiring acceptance of an invisible document is not a shippable state.

findings.title: Every custom select leaks a raw-value text field into the accessibility tree
findings.evidence: Beside each styled combobox sits an exposed textbox holding the machine value: 'textbox [ref=e320]: 06e3d009-7002-44ee-98db-9ef19a4ba294' under Human Onboarding Agent, 'textbox [ref=e332]: "yes"' under New Agent Greeting, 'textbox [disabled] [ref=e141]: admin' in the role picker (19-administration.aria.txt:166,176,89), and 'textbox [ref=e156]: all' beside the category filter (20-applications.aria.txt:102). None are labelled. Cost: a screen-reader user tabs past the Onboarding select into an unlabelled edit field and hears a 36-character UUID read out; the pattern adds a phantom field to every select in the cluster.
findings.recommendation: These are hidden form-value inputs never removed from the tree. Mark them `aria-hidden="true"` and `tabindex="-1"`, or move the value onto the combobox itself.

findings.title: Sidebar group labels — the entire IA taxonomy — are the least legible text on the screen
findings.evidence: "PERSONAL", "WORKSPACE" and "ABOUT" ('generic [ref=e55]: Personal', line 73 Workspace, line 94 About) measure #99968F on #FFFAEF = 2.84:1, small and letter-spaced. WCAG AA for normal text is 4.5:1. Cost: the Personal-vs-Workspace distinction is the single thing that tells a user whether a change affects only them or the whole team, and it is rendered below the legibility floor while the twelve item labels beneath it are near-black.
findings.recommendation: Bring group labels to at least 4.5:1 and increase their size, or replace the colour-only grouping with a visible divider plus a near-black label. The scope signal must be at least as legible as the item it scopes.

findings.title: The only confirmation that Appearance saved anything fails contrast and never announces
findings.evidence: "Saved on this device." ('generic [ref=e137]', 15-appearance.aria.txt:90, repeated at 113) measures #8C8C8C on #FFFFFF = 3.36:1, below the 4.5:1 AA floor, and is exposed as a plain generic — not a live region — so it never announces on change. Cost: in the one pane with no Save button, the sole evidence that a change persisted is dim, silent and easy to miss, leaving the user to toggle the control again to check.
findings.recommendation: Darken to at least 4.5:1 and make it a transient `role="status"` confirmation fired on change ("Font size set to Large — saved on this device") rather than a permanent grey caption carrying no event.

findings.title: Disabled-state and status text across Administration sit between 1.7:1 and 2.6:1
findings.evidence: Measured: "No members to promote" #C5C5C5 on #FFFFFF = 1.73:1 ('button "No members to promote" [disabled] [ref=e130]', line 81); "Last owner" #A4A4A4 on #FFFFFF = 2.49:1 (line 97); the disabled "Update Role" label 2.55:1. Cost: "Last owner" is the explanation for why the owner row has no remove control — the safety rationale is the hardest text on the pane to read — and "No members to promote", the pane's only empty-state message, is effectively invisible.
findings.recommendation: Disabled controls may drop to 3:1, but explanatory status text like "Last owner" is content, not a control — bring it to 4.5:1 and pair it with a lock or shield icon so the reason survives a low-contrast display.

findings.title: The promote-a-member empty state is expressed as a disabled control with no path forward
findings.evidence: The Add owner/admin row is entirely inert: 'button "No members to promote" [disabled] [ref=e130]', 'combobox [disabled] [ref=e135]' and 'button "Update Role" [disabled]' (19-administration.aria.txt:81-90). The pane shows exactly one owner marked "Last owner" and one agent admin. Nothing explains why there is nobody to promote (everyone present already holds a role), nothing links to Invite Links four sections below, and nothing states how a second owner is added. Cost: an admin cannot distinguish "no eligible members" from "broken" or "you lack permission", and the workspace stays at a bus factor of one with no visible remedy.
findings.recommendation: Replace the disabled row with a real empty state: "Everyone in this workspace already has a role. Invite a member to promote them." plus a link that scrolls to Invite Links. Where a second owner is the point, state explicitly how ownership is transferred.

findings.title: Documentation leaves the app from inside the nav with no external-link indication
findings.evidence: 'link "Documentation" [ref=e98] [cursor=pointer]' with '/url: https://docs.raft.build' (07-settings.aria.txt:61-64) is the only `link` among twelve nav `button`s, renders with a book icon and no ↗ glyph in the screenshot, and carries no target/rel disclosure in its accessible name. Cost: it sits one tab stop from Administration, a pane that can hold five sections of unsaved changes; a user reaching for in-app help navigates away and loses them.
findings.recommendation: Add a visible external-link glyph and "(opens in a new tab)" to the accessible name, open it in a new tab, and warn on navigation away from any pane with unsaved changes.

findings.title: Numeric inputs use different roles on different panes, and the one that sets the invoice is the weaker
findings.evidence: 'textbox "Seats to buy" [ref=e221]: "2"' on Billing (18-billing.aria.txt:149) versus 'spinbutton "Max Uses" [ref=e273]' on Administration (19-administration.aria.txt:130). Cost: the field that determines the invoice amount is a plain textbox — no arrow-key increment, no announced min/max, no exposed floor — even though the helper text asserts "Current usage requires at least 2 seats". A user typing 1 gets no constraint from the control itself.
findings.recommendation: Make Seats to buy a spinbutton with min set to the required floor and an inline error when violated, and keep stepper affordances identical across both panes.

findings.title: Visible field labels do not match their accessible names
findings.evidence: 'searchbox "Search connected apps" [ref=e148]' (20-applications.aria.txt:96) renders the placeholder "Search apps…" in the screenshot; 'combobox "Filter connected apps by category" [ref=e150]' renders "All categories". The visible string is not contained in the accessible name in either case. Cost: voice-control users saying "click Search apps" fail to hit the field (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name).
findings.recommendation: Make the accessible name start with the visible string — e.g. `aria-label="Search apps"` on the searchbox and a visible "Category" label above the combobox — so spoken and rendered labels agree.

findings.title: The Personal / Workspace / About split leaks in both directions
findings.evidence: Under Personal, Notifications contains a server-scoped control: "Mute this server — Stops web push notifications from raft-bobby-test for your account. Other servers are unchanged." (16-notifications.aria.txt:88). Under About, the second card is titled "Workspace" and repeats "raft-bobby-test / /raft-bobby-test" (22-about.aria.txt:137-140) — content already owned by Workspace → Server Profile. Meanwhile Delete Server lives in Server Profile, not Administration, where a user managing the workspace's lifecycle would look. Cost: users cannot use the group headings to predict where a setting lives or how far a change reaches, which is the only job those headings have.
findings.recommendation: Re-scope groups by blast radius, not subject: Personal = affects only me (including per-server mute, labelled as a personal preference), Workspace = affects everyone. Move Delete Server into Administration beneath the membership controls, and cut the Workspace card from About.

findings.title: 'Notifications' names three different things in the same accessibility tree
findings.evidence: 16-notifications.aria.txt simultaneously contains `button "Notifications" [ref=e68]` (settings nav), `heading "Notifications" [level=2] [ref=e117]` (the pane), and `region "Notifications"` (the toast container present on all 21 screens). A user navigating by landmark or by element list gets three unrelated hits for one word.
findings.recommendation: Rename the toast landmark to `aria-label="Alerts"` (or 'Toast messages') to free 'Notifications' for the settings feature.

findings.title: Persistent notification-permission banner is not exposed as a status region
findings.evidence: 01-chat-channel.aria.txt: `generic [ref=e1185]:` → `img [ref=e1186]`, `generic [ref=e1190]: Your agents keep working after you leave.`, `- text: Turn on notifications so you don't miss when they finish or need you.`, then `button "Enable notifications" [ref=e1193]` and `button "Hide notification reminder for this session" [ref=e1194]`. The advisory is a plain generic with an unnamed leading `img`, appended after the composer, so a keyboard user reaches it only after tabbing past the whole message input.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the banner in `role="region" aria-label="Notification setup"` (or `role="status"` when it first appears), mark the decorative icon `aria-hidden`, and place it before the composer in DOM order.

findings.title: Four different date formats across one channel, none of the visible ones carrying a year
findings.evidence: Message headers use `19/07 13:15` (01:116); date dividers use `Sunday 19 July` and `Tuesday 21 July` (01:108, 01:273); hover titles use `19 Jul 2026, 13:15` (01:141); the Files tab uses `19 Jul, 13:15` (12:114). Only the hover title reveals the year, and the content is dated 2026 — so a thread whose replies span years reads as if it happened this week.
findings.recommendation: Pick one short format for in-list timestamps and one long format for titles/tooltips, and use them on every surface. Include the year once the item is outside the current year; the Files tab and the message list should not disagree about how to write the same instant.

findings.title: Presence is painted retroactively onto historical messages
findings.evidence: All nine of Cindy's messages — dated 19 July and 21 July — carry the same `button "Offline"` / `generic "Offline"` avatar wrapper reflecting her state right now (01:110, 119, 133, 157, 171, 180, 196, 210, 233; 11 instances in 10-thread). Nothing in the row distinguishes "was offline when this was sent" from "is offline as you read this".
findings.recommendation: Presence is a now-fact; scope it to now. Show it on the member list, the sidebar entry, and at most the latest message, and leave historical rows unadorned.

findings.title: Disabled Send keeps the primary-button fill; the only disabled cue is a 1.64:1 icon
findings.evidence: `button "Send" [disabled]` (01:308). Sampled from the capture at x 1643–1680, y 814–851: fill rgb(255,216,229) with the paper-plane glyph at rgb(178,178,178) — 1.64:1 icon-on-fill — while the black border and pink fill of the enabled primary are retained. Visual read: "the contrast between the light pink background fill and the slightly darker pink icon is extremely low and appears well below the 3:1 ratio."
findings.recommendation: Give disabled Send a neutral fill and a visibly muted border so it stops reading as an armed primary, and keep the glyph legible against whatever fill you choose. If the composer is empty, a hint ("Type a message") is better feedback than a silent dead button.

findings.title: Composer has no way to address a specific agent
findings.evidence: The composer's complete control set is `button "Attach media"`, `button "Attach file"`, `checkbox "As Task"`, `button "Send"` (01:301-308). There is no mention button, emoji picker, formatting control, or slash-command affordance in any snapshot. In 14 the user has hand-typed `@Cindy` into `textbox "Message #onboarding-owner" [ref=e1173]` — the syntax is discoverable only by prior knowledge, in a product whose premise is channels containing several agents.
findings.recommendation: Add an `@` button that opens the same member picker used in Create Channel, and trigger the picker on typed `@`. Show matched agents with their presence state inline, so choosing an offline agent surfaces the offline fact at the moment of addressing.

findings.title: Thread composer silently loses the "As Task" control
findings.evidence: The channel composer exposes `checkbox "As Task" [ref=e1196]` (10:318-319, and 01:306). The thread composer, twelve lines later in the same snapshot, exposes only `textbox "Message thread"`, `button "Attach media"`, `button "Attach file"`, `button "Send" [disabled]` (10:376-385) — confirmed visually: "The `As Task` checkbox is **not** present in the thread composer."
findings.recommendation: Include As Task in the thread composer. Threads are where a request gets scoped down to something actionable; that is the point at which turning it into a task is most useful, and forcing a retype in the channel composer loses the thread linkage.

findings.title: Notification nudge can only be dismissed for the session and reserves 65px permanently
findings.evidence: The banner appears below the composer on every chat screen with `button "Enable notifications"` and `button "Hide notification reminder for this session" [ref=e1194]` (01:310-318). Measured at y 879–944 (65px) in a 960px window; the dismiss is explicitly session-scoped, so it returns on every visit until permissions are granted.
findings.recommendation: Offer a real "Don't show again" alongside the session dismiss, or collapse the nudge to a single-line inline affordance in the composer chrome after the first dismissal. Recurring 65px plus a recurring decision is a poor trade for a prompt the user has already declined.

findings.title: Member-count control is announced as "2"
findings.evidence: `button "2" [ref=e220]` containing `img [ref=e221]` and `generic [ref=e226]: "2"` (01:87-89, repeated on every chat screen). Its accessible name is the bare digit; the icon carries the meaning and has no text alternative.
findings.recommendation: `aria-label="Members (2)"`, and give the icon `aria-hidden="true"`.

findings.title: Grouped messages expose their timestamp twice to assistive tech
findings.evidence: Time-only continuation rows emit both the title string and the short label as sibling text nodes: `generic "19 Jul 2026, 13:15" [ref=e558]` followed by `generic [ref=e560]: 13:15` (01:141-142); same pattern at 01:189-190 (`"19 Jul 2026, 13:42"` / `13:42`) and 01:207-208 (`"19 Jul 2026, 13:50"` / `13:50`). A screen reader reads the instant twice per grouped message.
findings.recommendation: Use a `<time datetime>` element with the short form as its text and the long form on `title` only (or move the long form into `aria-label` on the element rather than as an adjacent text node), so exactly one timestamp reaches the accessibility tree.

findings.title: Channel traffic and DMs are separated only by a single small glyph
findings.evidence: Row 1 renders `# onboarding-owner`; row 2 renders `@ Cindy`. The rows are otherwise identical in layout, weight and colour, and the filter set (All / Unread / Mentions) offers no way to split channel from direct messages.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate the two sources visually beyond an 8px prefix glyph — a colour-coded source label or grouped sections — and consider adding a DMs facet to the filter group so the inbox can be triaged by source.

findings.title: The message preview repeats the sender named in the row header
findings.evidence: Row 2 header is `@ Cindy`; the preview immediately below opens with `generic [ref=e101]: "Cindy:"` before the message text.
findings.recommendation: Drop the sender prefix when the row header already identifies the sender (keep it for channel rows, where the header is the channel name and the sender is genuinely new information). The first words of a preview line are the highest-value scan position.

findings.title: The computers row announces 'offline' three times
findings.evidence: `button "Computer offline Bozhidars-MacBook-Air computer offline"` — the status icon's label (`generic "Computer offline" [ref=e61]`) plus the visible status text (`generic [ref=e66]: computer offline`) both feed the composed name.
findings.recommendation: Mark the status icon `aria-hidden` since its meaning is already in the visible text, yielding "Bozhidars-MacBook-Air, computer offline".

findings.title: The ⌘K hint is shown only when it is useless
findings.evidence: The placeholder reads "Search channels, DMs, messages…   ⌘K" on a field that is already focused (`textbox … [active] [ref=e57]`) on the Search destination itself.
findings.recommendation: Advertise ⌘K on the rail's Search button tooltip and in other destinations, not inside the field it opens. As placed, the shortcut is displayed only when the user has already done the thing it triggers, and it disappears the moment they start typing — shown when useless, hidden when learnable.

findings.title: Each pane states its own title three times; About states it five
findings.evidence: On 22-about the word About appears as the nav group label 'generic [ref=e94]: About', the nav item 'button "About" [ref=e95]', the topbar 'heading "About" [level=2] [ref=e116]', the section eyebrow, and the card title 'generic [ref=e125]: About' — five times above a two-line card. The same triple-titling recurs for Applications, MCP Servers, Appearance and Administration. Cost: roughly 80px of vertical space per pane spent restating the label the user just clicked.
findings.recommendation: Keep the topbar title and drop the eyebrow, or keep the eyebrow and drop the topbar. Where a pane has one section, the section title is redundant with the pane title — remove it and start with content.

findings.title: Section counts are concatenated to their labels in the accessibility tree
findings.evidence: 'generic [ref=e124]: Owners & Admins2' (19-administration.aria.txt:76), 'generic [ref=e125]: MCP servers0' (21-mcp.aria.txt:76), 'generic [ref=e144]: Recommended2' (line 90). The screenshots show a visual gap, so this is text-node concatenation rather than a rendering bug. Cost: screen readers announce "Owners and Admins two" and "MCP servers zero".
findings.recommendation: Separate the count into its own element with whitespace or an explicit label — e.g. "Owners & Admins" + `2 total` — so the announced string parses.

findings.title: Two identical Add server buttons in one viewport, and the same action carries different weight than on Applications
findings.evidence: 'button "Add server" [ref=e127]' in the header and 'button "Add server" [ref=e138]' in the empty state (21-mcp.aria.txt:77,85) are both visible simultaneously with identical labels and identical outline styling. The recommended-integration 'button "Add"' renders as a white/outline fill (sampled #FFFFFF) while the analogous Install on Applications is pink primary (#FE7DA8). Cost: minor redundancy plus a mismatched hierarchy — connecting an arbitrary credentialed HTTP endpoint is presented as a lower-emphasis action than installing a reviewed marketplace app.
findings.recommendation: Hide the header button while the empty state is showing, and align button weight to risk: give MCP's Add the same or greater emphasis as the marketplace Install.

findings.title: "More professional features coming soon" is listed as a missing feature with a red cross
findings.evidence: Under Not included: 'generic [ref=e185]: More professional features coming soon' with a cross icon, alongside three real limits (18-billing.aria.txt:117-119). Cost: on the upsell surface the implied Pro benefit is unspecified future work, which weakens the three concrete differentiators directly above it.
findings.recommendation: Remove the row from the comparison list. If a roadmap signal is wanted, put it below the plan card as prose, not as a crossed-out entitlement.

findings.title: Only the Marketplace tab shows a count
findings.evidence: 'radio "Marketplace 3" [checked]' carries a count while 'radio "Installed"' and 'radio "My apps"' carry none (20-applications.aria.txt:85-93). Cost: an admin cannot tell whether anything is installed on the server without clicking through, on a pane whose stated purpose includes "see apps installed on this server" (line 83).
findings.recommendation: Show counts on all three tabs, including a zero, so the tab strip answers "is anything installed?" without a round trip.
